newsitem.title: USA: Group backs vote for Sallie Mae dissidents.
newsitem.headline: Group backs vote for Sallie Mae dissidents.

text.p: A group that advises big shareholders in proxy contests Thursday recommended a vote for a dissident slate of directors opposed by the management of Student Loan Marketing Association, also known as Sallie Mae.

A shareholders vote is set for next Thursday on a plan to end Sallie Mae's status as a government-sponsored enterprise, and for directors supported by management or a rival slate from a group called the Committee To Restore Value, or CRV.
Sallie Mae is a government-sponsored, stockholder-owned agency that buys student loans from lenders and helps provide financing to state educational lending agencies.

According to the CRV, Institutional Shareholder Services said it favours the dissident group's strategic plan and management team. Institutonal Shareholder Services said Sallie Mae management has "managed to keep the Sallie Mae ship afloat but it has not demonstrated that it can do so without the CRV on board."
A group of CRV directors were elected to the Sallie Mae board in 1995 on a platform based on boosting its financial performance and stock price.
Albert Lord, a former Sallie Mae chief operating officer and chief financial officer, would become chief executive should the CRV slate win the election.
